$description: BIM KEY PLANS token category — authoritative catalog of all Woodfine Key Plan Compositions. A Key Plan is a Composition, not a BIM Object: a spatial program assembled from several BIM Objects (furniture, manufacturer SKUs) to satisfy a methodology, defined by a three-zone cross-section (Habitat / Magazine / Corridor), net leasable area, facade frontage, and accessibility compliance. Classified at Uniclass 2015 SL (Spaces-locations) level, distinct from the BIM Objects (Uniclass Pr/Ss level) it composes. Key Plans are authored by architects from Woodfine equipment programs; Key Plans nest into Tiles and Floor Plates without remainder, in both directions. IFC anchor: IfcSpace (each Key Plan is a bounded, named space within a floor storey — consistent with a Composition, not a product). Source: CONSTRUCTION_2026_01_06_Key Plan_Professional Office_FFE_FIN.xlsx — tab Summary_Key Plans (V3, 2025-11-29). Note: approximate square footages per source spreadsheet.

Building ID issued per desk. Habitat = 5.9944 m (19'-8"), marginally under the 6 m European Lighting Standard desk-to-window threshold. Magazine = 1.3716 m (4'-6"), holds filing, credenza, bookshelf. No Corridor — each office opens directly to the shared building corridor.
